How to Clean a Microwave: Effective and Natural Ways to Get the Job Done

Microwaves are one of the most used kitchen appliances in modern homes, yet they’re often one of the most neglected when it comes to cleaning. Whether you’re reheating leftovers or cooking meals, frequent use leads to inevitable spills and splatters, making the inside of the microwave a sticky, stained mess. Fortunately, you don’t need harsh chemicals to clean your microwave. With natural ingredients like lemon, vinegar, and baking soda, and by harnessing the power of steam, you can leave your microwave sparkling clean in just minutes.

In this guide, you’ll learn how to clean the inside of your microwave safely and effectively. From quick methods using household staples to deep-cleaning strategies for stubborn stains, we’ll cover everything you need to know to keep your microwave in top condition.

Why It’s Important to Clean Your Microwave

Over time, microwave splatter, spills, and stuck-on food debris build up inside your microwave, which can:

  • Produce unpleasant odors

  • Affect the flavor of your food

  • Harbor bacteria or mold

  • Reduce the efficiency of the appliance

Regular maintenance not only ensures hygiene but also prolongs the life of the microwave oven.

Best Ways to Clean a Microwave

There are many ways to clean a microwave, but the most effective methods use natural products and steam to loosen grime. Below are some tried-and-true techniques.

Use the Power of Steam and Lemon Juice

Why Lemon Works:

Lemon juice has natural antibacterial properties and a refreshing scent. Combined with the power of steam, it’s one of the best ways to clean your microwave without chemicals.

Instructions:

  1. Fill a microwave-safe bowl with 1 cup of water.

  2. Add the juice of one lemon (or a few slices).

  3. Place the bowl in the microwave.

  4. Run the microwave for 3 to 5 minutes on high power.

  5. Leave the door closed for another 2 minutes to let the steam loosen grime.

  6. Carefully remove the bowl (it will be hot).

  7. Wipe down the interior using a soft cloth, sponge, or paper towel.

This method is ideal for light to moderate cleaning and leaves a pleasant citrus smell.

Clean Your Microwave with Vinegar and Steam

Why Vinegar Works:

White vinegar is a natural disinfectant and odor neutralizer. It’s perfect for deep cleaning without damaging the microwave’s interior.

Instructions:

  1. Mix 1 cup water with 2 tablespoons of vinegar in a microwave-safe container.

  2. Microwave on high for 3–5 minutes, until the inside steams up.

  3. Leave the microwave door closed for a few minutes.

  4. Remove the bowl.

  5. Wipe down the microwave door, walls, and turntable.

Vinegar and steam are powerful allies against stuck-on food and microwave splatter.

Use Baking Soda to Scrub Away Stubborn Stains

If the inside of your microwave has tough spots or smells, baking soda is the answer.

Baking Soda Paste:

  1. Mix 2 tablespoons of baking soda with a bit of water to create a paste.

  2. Apply it to stuck-on food or stains.

  3. Let sit for 5–10 minutes.

  4. Scrub gently with a damp sponge or soft cloth.

  5. Rinse with soapy water and wipe down the interior.

Baking soda also absorbs odors, making your microwave clean and fresh.

Dish Soap and Water for Regular Cleaning

For everyday maintenance:

  1. Fill a microwave-safe bowl with soapy water (a few drops of mild dish soap in 1 cup of water).

  2. Heat for 2–3 minutes.

  3. Let the steam sit for a few more minutes.

  4. Remove the bowl.

  5. Use a damp cloth or sponge to clean the inside and microwave door.

This method is gentle yet effective for frequent wipe downs.

How to Clean the Microwave Turntable

Don’t forget the turntable, which catches a lot of food spills.

Instructions:

  1. Remove the turntable.

  2. Wash it in the sink with warm soapy water.

  3. Let it dry or wipe it dry with a soft cloth.

  4. Reinsert it after cleaning the rest of the microwave.

Deep Cleaning the Microwave Interior

Sometimes a dirty microwave needs more than just a quick wipe.

Step-by-Step Deep Clean:

  1. Unplug the appliance.

  2. Remove the turntable and any removable parts.

  3. Use the lemon and steam method (or vinegar).

  4. Apply baking soda paste to any remaining stuck-on areas.

  5. Use a sponge or soft cloth to scrub.

  6. Wipe all surfaces with a damp cloth.

  7. Dry thoroughly with a soft towel.

Make sure you check your microwave manual for any model-specific cleaning recommendations.

What Not to Use to Clean a Microwave

Avoid the following:

  • Harsh abrasives: Can scratch the surface

  • Metal scrubbers: Dangerous and damaging

  • Bleach: Overkill and may react with plastic

  • Flammable cleaners: Not safe for an enclosed, heated space

Stick to natural cleaners and gentle tools for safety and effectiveness.

How Often Should You Clean Your Microwave?

Light use: Once a week
Heavy use or visible splatter: Immediately after cooking
Deep cleaning: Once a month

Frequent small cleanings make deep cleaning easier and maintain the appliance’s longevity.

Microwave Cleaning Comparisons: Lemon vs Vinegar

Feature Lemon & Steam Vinegar & Steam
Scent Pleasant & fresh Strong but neutralizing
Cleaning Power Moderate High
Ease of Use Very Easy Very Easy
Odor Elimination Good Excellent
Residue Removal Good Very Good
Best For Light to medium mess Stubborn, sticky messes

Use lemon for lighter jobs or freshening. Choose vinegar for tougher grime.

Tips to Clean Less Often

  • Use a microwave-safe cover to prevent microwave splatter.

  • Wipe the inside of the microwave after every few uses.

  • Cover foods that are likely to spill.

  • Don’t let food sit—clean the inside immediately after use.

  • Keep a microwave-safe bowl with a bit of baking soda inside when not in use to absorb smells.

Safe Products You Can Use to Clean

  • Lemon juice or vinegar

  • Baking soda

  • Mild dish soap

  • Soapy water

  • Water and lemon

  • Microwave-safe glass containers

  • Paper towels, soft cloth, or sponge

These items are inexpensive, safe, and readily available in most homes.

Additional Cleaning Recommendations

  • Clean around the microwave door seals for hygiene.

  • Use glass cleaner only on the outside of the door, never inside.

  • If your microwave has vents, clean them with a damp sponge.

  • Avoid opening the door mid-cycle during steaming to trap heat.

  • Let steam sit with the door closed before wiping to loosen debris.

How to Keep Your Microwave Sparkling Clean

Once clean, help it stay that way:

  • Wipe down surfaces weekly.

  • Use microwave-safe lids or covers.

  • Clean spills right away.

  • Avoid overfilling containers that might boil over.

  • Perform a deep cleaning monthly using lemon, vinegar, or baking soda.

A few minutes of upkeep weekly keeps your microwave’s interior clean and odor-free.

FAQ: How to Clean a Microwave

What is the best way to clean a microwave?

The best way to clean a microwave naturally is by using steam from lemon or vinegar water. Place 1 cup of water with either lemon slices or 2 tablespoons of vinegar in a microwave-safe bowl, heat for 3–5 minutes, let steam sit, and then wipe down.

Can I use dish soap to clean my microwave?

Yes. Mix a few drops of mild dish soap in 1 cup of water, microwave for a couple of minutes, and let the steam loosen grime before wiping.

How do I clean microwave splatter?

Use the power of steam by heating water and lemon juice or vinegar in the microwave. Let the steam soften the splatter, then wipe it clean with a soft cloth or sponge.

Is it safe to clean with baking soda?

Absolutely. Baking soda is a safe, non-toxic cleaner. Use it as a paste or to deodorize the interior. Just ensure you rinse thoroughly.

How often should I clean my microwave?

Wipe down weekly, and do a deep cleaning monthly. If you see or smell residue, clean immediately.

Can I use glass cleaner inside the microwave?

No. Use glass cleaner only on the outside of the microwave door. For the interior, stick to natural or microwave-safe cleaners like vinegar, lemon, or dish soap.

What if the inside smells bad?

Heat a bowl with water and lemon or vinegar to deodorize. You can also leave a bowl of baking soda inside (when not in use) to absorb odors.

Can I clean the microwave with bleach?

It’s not recommended. Bleach is too harsh and can leave harmful residue or react with the plastic interior. Stick to natural alternatives.

How do I clean the turntable?

Remove it and wash with warm soapy water, or place in the dishwasher if safe. Dry thoroughly before returning.

Is steaming safe for all microwave models?

Generally, yes. Always check your microwave manual for any specific cleaning recommendations.

Cleaning your microwave doesn’t have to be a chore or require harsh chemicals. With simple household items like lemon, vinegar, and baking soda, and by taking advantage of the power of steam, you can clean the inside of your microwave efficiently and naturally. Whether it’s a quick wipe down or a full deep cleaning, these methods help keep your appliance fresh, functional, and ready for your next meal.
